title: The conjecture that a gamma-function expression is logarithmically completely monotonic
statement:
Let $\psi$ denote the digamma function, let $\gamma$ denote the Euler–Mascheroni constant, and define

$$
q(t):=t^{t(\psi(t)-\log t)-\gamma}.
$$

**Logarithmic complete monotonicity conjecture.** The function $q$ is logarithmically completely monotonic on $(0,\infty)$; that is,

$$
(-1)^n[\log q(t)]^{(n)}\geq 0
$$

for every $t>0$ and every integer $n\geq 1$.
This conjecture concerns the relationship between completely monotonic and logarithmically completely monotonic functions, with the latter forming a subclass of the former. The supplied text attributes the conjecture to an earlier work but gives no evidence of a resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00124

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).
source_name: Valmir Krasniqi and Armend Sh. Shabani, “On a conjecture of a logarithmically completely monotonic function”, arXiv:1601.00124 (2016).
